subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.

spec.name: Calder Mobile in Red, Yellow, Blue and Black
spec.description: A hanging abstract mobile in the manner of Alexander Calder: thin black wire arms in three balanced tiers, each arm hung from the end of another, carrying flat painted sheet-metal discs, leaves and a bean in primary red, yellow, blue, black and white.
spec.layout: A single mobile hanging from a small ceiling cap and hook at the top (y 2.6). It is NOT standing on the floor: the lowest sheet-metal shapes float with their bottoms at y 0.02 to 0.1, and the cap at y 2.6 to 2.7 is the highest point. A thin black wire runs down to a long horizontal top arm (arm1, y 2.25, from x -0.95 to x +0.6, pivot at x 0). Each end of arm1 hangs a plain wire down to the pivot of a second-tier arm. On the model's left (+X) arm2 hangs at (0.6,1.7,0). It is yawed about 40 degrees so it reaches forward and back (z -0.32 to +0.58). It carries a big red disc on its back end and a long wire from its front end down to the small lowest-tier arm4 at (1.29,0.9,0.58). Arm4 carries a tall black leaf and a small red ball. On the model's right (-X) arm3 hangs at (-0.95,1.55,0), yawed about -30 degrees. It carries a yellow bean on its short end and a long wire from its other end down to arm5 at (-0.38,0.75,-0.33). Arm5 carries a large blue disc at the back and a small black leaf at the front. The silhouette is asymmetric and airy, wide and sparse, with arms spread in x and in depth (z) so it reads in 3D from any side. Style: every arm is a thin wire rod (radius 0.006), the hanging wires are thinner (0.004), and every joint between a wire and an arm is a small tight loop (a thin torus or ring of radius about 0.015) with a tiny knot. Every shape is a flat sheet of painted metal, extruded about 0.012 m thick with a slight bevel, hung from one point on its upper edge through a small wire eyelet, and tilted or rolled a different amount (10 to 35 degrees) so the shapes catch the light unevenly. Each shape has a slightly darker thin rim strip or a pale highlight sliver as separate small parts, and a little black wire hook at its hanging point. Arm ends have tiny bead counterweights or small bent-wire hooks. Everything is flat colour and low-poly (6 to 10 sided wires and circles, 16 to 24 sided discs). Nothing else exists: no stand, ground or room.

parts.builds: The top of the mobile. A small ceiling cap: a flat lathe disc (radius 0.08, cap colour with a capDark rim ring and 2 tiny screw heads) with a short wire hook and an eye loop below it at hookEye. A thin wire runs from the hook down to the arm1 pivot and ties on with a small loop and knot. Arm1 itself: a thin black wire rod from arm1EndRight (-0.95,2.25,0) to arm1EndLeft (0.6,2.25,0) with small bead counterweights (black spheres, radius 0.02) at both ends and a little loop at the pivot. Each end has a loop, and a plain thin wire hangs from it down to the next arm's pivot: from arm1EndLeft straight down to arm2Pivot (0.6,1.7,0), and from arm1EndRight straight down to arm3Pivot (-0.95,1.55,0). Those wires finish in small loops at the pivots. Extra detail on the arm: one small black leaf (an extruded smooth outline about 0.22 long and 0.1 wide, 0.012 thick, black with a blackLight sliver highlight, rolled about 20 degrees) hanging from a short wire (0.3 long) at x -0.35 on arm1, hanging from a small bent-wire hook, with its bottom at about y 1.7. Also a very small white disc (radius 0.05) hanging 0.25 below arm1 at x 0.25 on a thin wire, rolled 25 degrees. Colours: wire, wireHighlight, cap, capDark, black, blackLight, white. Everything rides the joints mobile (cap, hook, top wire) and arm1 (the arm, its end loops, the hanging wires and the small shapes).
parts.attaches: The wire ends at the arm2Pivot and arm3Pivot mounts, where the branch parts' own pivot loops begin. The cap is the highest point of the model.

parts.builds: The second-tier arm on the left side (+X), arm2, hanging from arm2Pivot with a small loop and a knot at the top. The arm is a thin black wire rod from arm2EndBack (0.215,1.7,-0.32) to arm2EndFront (1.293,1.7,0.576), yawed about 40 degrees, with a loop and a bead at each end. From arm2EndBack a thin wire hangs 0.4 down to a big red disc, 0.2 radius (low-poly circle of 20 sides, extruded 0.012, red) hung from a small eyelet on its upper rim and tilted about 25 degrees. It has a darker redDark rim strip, a redLight highlight crescent on its upper face, a small black wire hook, and a thin concentric ring of redDark as a printed line. The disc's centre is at about y 1.1. From arm2EndFront a long thin wire hangs straight down 0.8 to arm4Pivot (1.29,0.9,0.58), ending in a small loop. Also hang a small blue-dark ball (radius 0.06, blue) from arm2 about a third of the way toward the back end on a thin wire 0.25 long, with a blueLight glint speck. Colours: wire, wireHighlight, red, redDark, redLight, blue, blueLight, black. Everything rides the joint arm2.
parts.attaches: Top loop at arm2Pivot (below crown's wire); the long wire from arm2EndFront ends at arm4Pivot where branchLeftLower begins.

parts.builds: The lowest tier on the left, arm4, hanging from arm4Pivot with a loop and a knot. A short thin black wire rod from arm4EndBack (0.91,0.9,0.72) to arm4EndFront (1.76,0.9,0.41), yawed about -20 degrees, with a loop and a bead at each end. From arm4EndBack a 0.3 long wire hangs down to a tall black leaf-shaped sheet (about 0.5 long and 0.2 wide, a smooth pointed leaf outline extruded 0.012 thick, black with a blackLight highlight sliver along one edge and a fine white vein line), hung from its top tip so that its bottom is at about y 0.1, rolled about 30 degrees. From arm4EndFront a 0.2 long wire hangs down to a small red ball (a sphere of radius 0.1, red, with a redDark underside cap and a redLight glint) at about y 0.55, and a small white bead on the wire above it. Colours: wire, wireHighlight, black, blackLight, white, red, redDark, redLight. Everything rides the joint arm4. Its lowest point is the bottom of the black leaf at y 0.1.
parts.attaches: Hangs from the end of branchLeftUpper's wire at arm4Pivot.

parts.builds: The whole right side (-X) of the mobile, arm3 and arm5 and what they carry. Arm3 hangs from arm3Pivot (-0.95,1.55,0) with a loop and knot. Its thin black wire rod runs from arm3EndShort (-1.428,1.55,0.275) to arm3EndLong (-0.384,1.55,-0.325), yawed about -30 degrees, with loops and beads at the ends. From arm3EndShort a 0.4 wire hangs to a yellow bean (a kidney-shaped extruded outline about 0.4 long and 0.2 wide, 0.012 thick, yellow, with a yellowDark rim strip, a yellowLight highlight and a small black eyelet and hook), rolled about 35 degrees, bottom at about y 0.85. From arm3EndLong a long wire hangs down 0.8 to arm5Pivot (-0.38,0.75,-0.33) with a loop. Arm5 is a thin wire rod from arm5EndBack (-0.58,0.75,-0.68) to arm5EndFront (-0.205,0.75,-0.03), yawed about 60 degrees, with loops and beads. From arm5EndBack a 0.2 wire hangs to a large blue disc (radius 0.27, 24 sides, extruded 0.012, blue, with a blueDark rim strip, a blueLight highlight crescent, and a black wire hook) tilted about 20 degrees, its bottom at about y 0.02. From arm5EndFront a 0.35 wire hangs to a small black leaf (about 0.3 long, 0.12 wide, black with a blackLight highlight) with its bottom at about y 0.1, rolled about -20 degrees. Colours: wire, wireHighlight, yellow, yellowDark, yellowLight, blue, blueDark, blueLight, black, blackLight. Arm3 and its yellow bean ride joint arm3; arm5 and everything below it ride joint arm5. The lowest point is the blue disc at y about 0.02.
parts.attaches: Top loop at arm3Pivot (below crown's wire); arm5 hangs from arm3EndLong at arm5Pivot.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out how to spec a Calder-style hanging mobile, which hangs from the ceiling rather than standing on the floor. The open question is what the lowest point should be, since the floor-contact rule doesn't map cleanly onto something suspended.

I'm settling on a lowest point around y=0.1 so the mobile hangs just above the floor, with the top hook near 2.5. Since nothing hangs above the model's top, the ceiling hook sits clear of the structure. Next I'm deciding whether to use joints for rotation, so I'll pick rigid arms with hinge joints at each pivot.

I'm laying out the arms of the mobile now: the top arm pivots at the center, with a small black leaf hanging from one end and a wire running down from the other to the second level. The second arm is angled in both x and z so it swings out in depth, and I'm fixing its endpoints in coordinates.

I'm splitting the build by part, starting with the top section: the ceiling cap, the hook, and the first arm with the blades hanging from its ends. Arms can be given as lines in the joints, with the builders working out the pivot positions along each one.

I'm laying out the rest of the mobile's tree now: a second-level arm and a lower arm, with a sub-mobile on the opposite side. I'm defining the root joint at the top and the first arm as a hinge that runs along x, with its weight placed closer to the fulcrum.

I'm placing the top arm at y=2.25, with its right end hanging the heavier branch near x=-0.95 and its left end at x=0.6 dropping a wire to the second-level joint. The third branch hangs lower on the right side from there.

I'm working out the coordinates for the second arm, which is angled so it extends in both x and z. I'm placing its endpoints roughly between x=0.2 and x=1.3 at height 1.7, then checking how far the shapes at each end will reach outward.

I'm fixing the sizing of the mobile at roughly 3.0 by 2.7 by 2.0 and getting the back end of the second arm to hang a wire down to a red disc. The front end drops a longer wire to a lower joint, where the small shapes will go.

I'm placing the third arm on the right branch, angled back in z, and working out its two endpoints so the hanging parts can attach near each end.

I'm checking whether the lowest disc can clear the floor. Working the arithmetic through, a disc of radius 0.28 hung from a wire attached at y=0.35 would have its centre near 0.07, which dips below the y=0.1 minimum I set.

I'm settling the lowest disc so it stays just above the floor: a wire of about 0.2 from the arm leaves its top near 0.55, which puts the centre around 0.27 and its bottom close to zero. I also want to add a small black leaf hanging near the pivot of the top arm, and then split the build into parts, with the crown holding the hook, the cap, and the wires down to the lower arms.

I'm sketching out the split into parts now: the crown gets the arm at the top with a small black leaf and a red counterweight, while the two lower branches get their own arms and hanging shapes. I'm still weighing whether a fourth part makes the budgets more even.

I'm placing the fourth arm at the lower front end of the left branch, and working out its ends so the lowest shapes sit just above the floor. The leaf hangs from one end on a short wire, with its top near 0.6 so its bottom reaches about 0.1, and the other end gets a shorter wire.

I'm settling the size of the mobile at about 3.8 by 2.7 by 1.9, and I'll check whether the x range needs shifting so it stays centred. The small red ball near the lower arm will hang at about y=0.55, and the yellow shape on the far right sits just beyond the blade there.

I'm defining the joints for the mobile's tree: a root at the top, with the first arm hinged along x beneath it and its two ends dropping wires to the second and third arms.

I'm working through the joint layout for the mobile's tree, with the root at the top and the first arm hinged along x beneath it. The lower arms will ride on the joints at the ends of the arms above them.

Next I'm checking the arm pivots against their endpoints, confirming the second arm's joint lines up with the ends I computed, and placing the fourth arm's pivot at the front of the second.

I'm working out the endpoints of the fifth arm, with its two ends placed near the blue disc and a small pale shape to finish the lower branch.

I'm finishing the mounting points for the right branch and the upper left arm. The right branch gets a blue-and-black section near its lower arm, and the upper left arm carries a red disc hung on a short wire.

I'm settling on a palette of black wire, red, yellow, blue, and white, with darker shades of red, yellow, and blue for the rim edges. Each shape will be a thin extruded outline with a small eyelet at its hanging point.

Now I'm writing the JSON spec itself, with each part described in detail along with its coordinates.
